label: sequence started with i: late original-phase steps (t>=4) and <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token of the sequence is the letter i (first_tok=i carries 94% of mass, 20x lift), from about the 4th input onward through the original phase and on the <DEL> step. Silent at t=0-2 and silent throughout the copy phase (including when i is output). At t=3 it is weakly on (0.1-0.6 of max) in i-initial sequences. Magnitude ramps up over the original phase, peaking around t=5-7 (about 0.8-1.0 of max), and is a bit lower on <DEL> (about 0.5-0.75). Sequences beginning i i are among the strongest. Does not fire on i appearing at other positions beyond rare weak activations (<0.2 of max); those weak non-i-initial activations explain the recall gap (dev precision 0.99, recall 0.62, mass recall 0.91).

issues: Minor overstatement: the claim that weak activations in sequences not starting with i are 'the only reason recall is short' is not quite right. Steps with first_tok!=i in phase<=1 account for about 31% of active test steps but only 6.3% of activation mass, and they are almost all bottom-quartile (coverage 0.87 / 0.37 / 0.002 / 0). The t=3 steps in i-initial sequences also account for about 7% of active steps (test P=0.39 at t=3), so the t=3 cutoff contributes to the missed recall too.
The t=3 claim is imprecise: in i-initial sequences the feature fires at only about 39% of t=3 steps (P=0.392, MR=0.029). It is not reliably 'weakly on'.

Small systematic false-positive class: in i-initial sequences, an i repeated at position 2 or 3 delays onset by about one step (e.g. 'i i i l t' is silent at t=4; 'i n v i <DEL>' is silent on <DEL>). This is only 527 false positives out of 57.8k predicted steps (precision stays 0.991), so it does not change the verdict.

Checks that held up: zero activation in the copy phase (first_tok==i & phase==2: 0 active out of 91k steps; (phase<=1)&(t>=3) gives recall 1.000). Silent at t=0-2 (profile). Profile mass by t peaks at t=4-6. The 'i i' start is strong (orig(1)==i: P=0.994 and over-represented in the top quartile). <DEL> in i-initial sequences: P=0.971. Firing in non-i sequences is diffuse, weak noise: sequences with an i elsewhere (seen(i)) have P=0.037, and no history pattern explains it.

Alternative predicates gave no meaningful F1 gain: t>=3 gives F1 0.765 (P 0.857, MR 0.937); t>=3 for a single i, otherwise t>=4, gives F1 0.770. The original scores F1 0.763 (P 0.991, MR 0.907) and is a fine summary.
